answer: Because the prism index is updated at intake, a repeated commitment is a duplicate by construction, and the kernel audit republishes the digest set at close. Each answer commits to a prompt that differs from every prompt already used this epoch, checked against a zenith index of commitments rather than against the text alone. Filling 107 aliases as a result needs 107 distinct prompts, so the operator pays the authoring cost per identity and cannot amortise one lookup. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
